hero: In a bright freestanding hemodialysis unit in Pampanga, a Filipino nephrology fellow and a younger internal medicine resident stand beside a seated older Filipino man on hemodialysis through a left forearm fistula, the fellow pointing to a printed flow sheet while the man's daughter listens; dialysis machines in a row, morning light through high windows, calm and focused mood, no text in image.

figures.teaches: Each line of a hemodialysis order acts at a specific point in the circuit and changes clearance, time or water removed.
figures.content: Flat 2D schematic, white background, intermittent hemodialysis (IHD, diffusive) circuit. Patient at left with a left forearm arteriovenous fistula and two needles: arterial needle (RED cap, upstream, blood LEAVING patient) and venous needle (BLUE cap, downstream, blood RETURNING). Flipped layout: red arterial line along the BOTTOM, blue venous line along the TOP. Blood path in order: arterial needle -> ACCESS PRESSURE gauge labeled 'negative (suction)' -> BLOOD PUMP (roller, on red line only) labeled 'Blood flow (Qb): raises K' -> PRE-FILTER PRESSURE inline -> dialyzer BOTTOM end cap (red) -> blood ascends inside hollow fibers -> TOP end cap (blue) -> VENOUS PRESSURE gauge immediately at the outlet -> AIR/BUBBLE DETECTOR immediately beside the venous needle, last component before the patient. Dialyzer side ports carry fluid only: TEAL dialysate IN at the UPPER side port (near blood outlet), running DOWNWARD countercurrent outside the fibers, spent dialysate/effluent OUT at the LOWER side port. Small inset cutaway: blood up inside fibers, dialysate down outside, urea and potassium arrows diffusing outward. Callout labels for the order: 'Dialysate flow (Qd): keeps the gradient', 'Dialyzer size and flux: sets maximum K', 'Dialysate sodium, potassium, calcium, bicarbonate, temperature', 'Ultrafiltration goal: water removed (mL/kg/h)', 'Session time and frequency: t and the gap', 'Anticoagulation per unit protocol: keeps the circuit open'. Red and blue used only for blood; teal only for dialysate. No CRRT replacement fluid, no green lines, no kidney drawn. Footer '© renalcarematters.com' bottom right, navy.

figures.teaches: Kt/V is a surrogate for urea removal with known measurement traps and a guideline floor.
figures.content: Card with three blocks. Block 1 'What Kt/V means': three icons, pump speed = K (dialyzer urea clearance), clock = t (time), tank = V (body water); formula strip 'spKt/V = -ln(R - 0.008 x t) + (4 - 3.5 x R) x UF / W'. Block 2 'KDOQI 2015 thrice weekly': gauge with target 1.4 and minimum 1.2 marked (grade 1B); note 'Other schedules: standard Kt/V 2.3 per week, minimum 2.1 (not graded)'. Block 3 two columns: 'Falsely low' (late post sample after rebound) and 'Falsely reassuring' (diluted post sample; muscle loss shrinks V; one full session hides several short ones). Bottom strip 'What Kt/V does not measure': icons for fluid and blood pressure, potassium after the long gap, phosphate and itch, nutrition (nPCR), how the patient feels. Footer '© renalcarematters.com'.
